record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: Let gamma_k=1/(k+1)^(k+1) for k>=0. Determine whether the sequence {gamma_k/k!}_{k>=0}={1/((k+1)^(k+1) k!)}_{k>=0} is a classical multiplier sequence, and determine whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence. A classical multiplier sequence preserves real-rootedness under the diagonal operator T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k; a CZDS is a sequence whose diagonal operator does not increase the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial.

evidence.quote: Problem 43. Let gamma_k := 1/(k + 1)^(k+1), k in N_0. Determine whether the sequence {gamma_k/k!}_0^infinity is (a) a multiplier sequence (b) a CZDS.
We conclude this paper with one more open problem that (i) may be useful in the study of CZDS and (ii) is related to our results in Section 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real sequence $\{\lambda_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a (classical) multiplier sequence if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$ whose zeros are all real, the polynomial $T[p](x):=\sum_{k=0}^n \lambda_k a_k x^k$ also has only real zeros. A real sequence $\{\lambda_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$, the number of nonreal zeros of $T[p](x)=\sum_{k=0}^n \lambda_k a_k x^k$ (counted with multiplicities) does not exceed the number of nonreal zeros of $p(x)$.

For $k\ge 0$, set
$$\gamma_k := \frac{1}{(k+1)^{k+1}},$$
and consider the sequence
$$\left\{\frac{\gamma_k}{k!}\right\}_{k\ge 0} = \left\{\frac{1}{(k+1)^{k+1}\, k!}\right\}_{k\ge 0}.$$

(a) Determine whether $\{\gamma_k/k!\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a classical multiplier sequence.

(b) Determine whether $\{\gamma_k/k!\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a complex zero decreasing sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific problem was located. The problem is posed as an open problem in the theory of multiplier sequences and CZDS, and searches did not turn up a subsequent paper resolving either part (a) or (b).
